problem: The exponents are lost: the text reads "N=1012 needs about 106 Grover steps, not 1012", which literally says N equals one thousand and twelve and that Grover needs only 106 steps.
fix: \"N=10<sup>12</sup> needs about 10<sup>6</sup> Grover steps, not 10<sup>12</sup>\" (about (π/4)·10<sup>6</sup> ≈ 7.9×10<sup>5</sup>, so \"about 10<sup>6</sup>\" is right).

problem: "N=2n" is written without the exponent, so it reads as N = 2 times n. The definition N = 2 to the power n is the basis of the whole chapter (n qubits, N items), and a student will misread it.
fix: Write \"N=2<sup>n</sup>\" everywhere; also write the circuit in Section 2 with the superscript clearly, H<sup>⊗n</sup>(2|0⟩⟨0|−I)H<sup>⊗n</sup>.

problem: The exponent is lost again: "For a search space of size 2m, Grover still needs about 2m/2 queries" reads as size 2m and 2m/2 = m queries, which is wrong and destroys the point of the answer.
fix: \"For a search space of size 2<sup>m</sup>, Grover still needs about 2<sup>m/2</sup> queries.\"

problem: Two plotted points do not match P(k)=sin²((2k+1)θ) with θ=0.252680 rad: the plot gives P(4)=0.585 (true value 0.5817) and P(5)=0.124 (true value 0.1255). The other points (0.0625, 0.472, 0.908, 0.961, 0.020) are correct.

"After the oracle, the marked amplitude is negative and all other amplitudes are positive" and "turns each unmarked amplitude slightly smaller" are true only for the first iteration. Later, once (2k+1)θ passes π/2, the unmarked amplitude cos((2k+1)θ) turns negative, so the signs described are wrong mid-search.
fix: Say \"In the first iteration, after the oracle the marked amplitude is 1/√N in magnitude and negative...\", and describe the later behaviour in Section 3 where the rotation picture is introduced.

problem: Cross-reference mismatch: Section 4 says quantum counting and the √N lower bound are in 4.8, but Q8 sends the reader to 4.9 for the same limitation topic.
fix: Point Q8 to the chapter that actually discusses the limits of Grover (4.8), or state plainly what is in 4.9.
